title: Each text builds on the last
statement: Each text in a unit should need only knowledge an earlier text added or the unit states as entry knowledge.
example: In one four-text unit the last text assumes four knowledge items, all added by the three texts before it.
detail: A four-text knowledge-building unit was designed from an inventory of what each text assumes and adds, each item tied to the words that carry it, with the entry knowledge the theme assumes and a check that every text's assumptions are covered by earlier texts or entry knowledge, with no forward references (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/00-knowledge-inventory.md`). Its texts ramp from primer to build to deepen to a transfer text with less topical overlap and the same schema (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/00-difficulty-notes.md`), and the unit is assessed on an unseen text that exercises the schema, teaches nothing new and avoids the curriculum-staple example (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/phase-e/capstone/passage.md`). A review of a story course checks the same thing for characters and places, each introduced before its first use (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/lens-arc-continuity.md`). The unit's test should be an unseen text that uses the same knowledge on a new surface and teaches nothing new; in that unit the transfer text adds four knowledge items on the same schema and the test text adds none.
against: A sandbox design, not approved doctrine: the inventory says not to promote its candidate ids or sandbox spine into approved curriculum doctrine (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/00-knowledge-inventory.md`).

evidence.quote: Proposed adds / assumes per text, with carrying spans.
